subject: Non-uniqueness of eigenvectors and implications for initializing model

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Non-uniqueness of eigenvectors and implications for initializing model
parts:
I'm working on a model to analyze some ordinal (Likert-scale) survey data and I'm having difficulties creating good initial values, where good means "the joint probability doesn't round down to 0."  At a high level, the model looks something like this:
  • N = # of individuals
  • M = # of questions
  • K = # of levels
  • z is an M x N array of latent responses (modeled)
  • zeta is an M-vector giving the prior mean for z[,i] (modeled)
  • Sigma is an M x M matrix giving the prior covariance for z[,i] (modeled)
  • cutp is an ordered vector of cutpoints used to translate each z[i,j] into an ordinal response x[i,j] (modeled)
A computational difficulty here is handling the likelihood for an individual's array of ordinal responses x[,i], which is the integral of an M-dimensional multivariate normal density over a rectangular region. The straightforward data augmentation using z doesn't work well (difficult to program in Stan, and very slow mixing), so I'm using a covariance decomposition approach. I end up with something that looks like this:

    xi[j, i] ~ Normal(0, 1)
    z[ , i] ~ MultivariateNormal(zeta + A * xi[ , i], D)

where
  • D is a diagonal matrix
  • A is a function of D and the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix R*
  • R* is a function of D and another matrix R
  • R + D = Sigma.
This allows me to integrate out the z[,i], giving a likelihood conditional on R, D, and xi that is the product of univariate normal CDFs.

I'm using an R script to generate reasonable initial values for the model variables. To get reasonable values for xi requires reproducing some of the computations used to produce that A matrix, including the computation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of R*.

There's the rub: I cannot reproduce in R the computation of the A matrix, because the eigendecomposition is not unique. Even if there are no repeated eigenvalues, and you normalize the eigenvectors, and you use a standard ordering of eigenvectors based on the eigenvalues, you can still multiply any subset of the eigenvectors by -1 and get another, equally valid, set of eigenvectors. There's no way I know of to guarantee that I'll get the same set of eigenvectors in R as I get in Stan.

If anyone has any ideas for dealing with this problem, I would be very happy to hear them.

You could use RcppEigen and some C++ to do the eigendecomposition via Eigen from R.

Or you could flip things around so that the first row of the eigenvector matrix is strictly positive in both R and Stan.

Ben
